name: All-Purpose Flour
note: All-purpose flour can compact in its bag. Fluff it first, spoon it gently into a dry measuring cup, then level the top without tapping or pressing. Scooping directly with the cup often adds more flour than a recipe expects. A kitchen scale gives more repeatable results for baking.

faq.q: Why does all-purpose flour weigh differently by cup?
faq.a: Brand, particle size, moisture, and how the cup is filled can change the result.

faq.q: Should I use a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Yes, a scale is the most repeatable option when baking precision matters.

name: Bread Flour
note: Bread flour is a higher-protein wheat flour used for chewy loaves and pizza dough. Spoon it into the measuring cup and level it rather than packing it down. Milling and storage can change how much fits in a cup, so use the weight in your recipe when available.

faq.q: Why does bread flour weigh differently by cup?
faq.a: Brand, particle size, moisture, and how the cup is filled can change the result.

faq.q: Should I use a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Yes, a scale is the most repeatable option when baking precision matters.

name: Granulated Sugar
note: Granulated sugar generally settles more consistently than flour, but crystal size and cup shape still matter. Fill a dry measuring cup and level it without pressing the sugar down. For large batches or precise baking ratios, weighing the sugar is the most repeatable approach.

faq.q: Why does granulated sugar weigh differently by cup?
faq.a: Brand, particle size, moisture, and how the cup is filled can change the result.

faq.q: Should I use a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Yes, a scale is the most repeatable option when baking precision matters.

name: Brown Sugar
note: Brown sugar is commonly measured packed because its moist crystals hold their shape. Press it into the cup if your recipe says firmly packed, unless the recipe specifies a loose measure. Moisture level and whether the sugar is light or dark can change the final weight.

faq.q: Why does brown sugar weigh differently by cup?
faq.a: Brand, particle size, moisture, and how the cup is filled can change the result.

faq.q: Should I use a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Yes, a scale is the most repeatable option when baking precision matters.

name: Powdered Sugar
note: Powdered sugar is finely milled and may contain anti-caking starch. Sifting loosens it and changes how much fits in a cup, so follow the recipe's sifted or unsifted instruction. Weighing is the most consistent option when exact proportions matter.

faq.q: Why does powdered sugar weigh differently by cup?
faq.a: Brand, particle size, moisture, and how the cup is filled can change the result.

faq.q: Should I use a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Yes, a scale is the most repeatable option when baking precision matters.

name: Butter
note: Butter has a relatively consistent weight and many US wrappers mark tablespoons and cup fractions. One US cup is commonly treated as two standard sticks, about 227 grams. If a recipe specifies melted butter, follow whether the amount is measured before or after melting.

faq.q: Why does butter weigh differently by cup?
faq.a: Brand, particle size, moisture, and how the cup is filled can change the result.

faq.q: Should I use a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Yes, a scale is the most repeatable option when baking precision matters.

name: Honey
note: Honey is much denser than water, so a cup weighs substantially more than a cup of water. Density varies with temperature and water content. Lightly coat the measuring cup to help honey release, and weigh it when precision matters.

faq.q: Why does honey weigh differently by cup?
faq.a: Brand, particle size, moisture, and how the cup is filled can change the result.

faq.q: Should I use a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Yes, a scale is the most repeatable option when baking precision matters.

name: Milk
note: Milk weighs slightly more than the same volume of water because it contains dissolved sugars, proteins, fat, and minerals. Use a liquid measuring jug on a level surface and read the line at eye level. Fat content and product formulation can cause small differences.

faq.q: Why does milk weigh differently by cup?
faq.a: Brand, particle size, moisture, and how the cup is filled can change the result.

faq.q: Should I use a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Yes, a scale is the most repeatable option when baking precision matters.

name: Cocoa Powder
note: Cocoa powder is light and can compact during storage. Fluff it, spoon it into the measuring cup, and level the surface rather than dipping the cup into the container. Natural and Dutch-process cocoa may differ, so use recipe-specific values when available.

faq.q: Why does cocoa powder weigh differently by cup?
faq.a: Brand, particle size, moisture, and how the cup is filled can change the result.

faq.q: Should I use a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Yes, a scale is the most repeatable option when baking precision matters.

name: Rolled Oats
note: Rolled oats contain air spaces between flakes, so cup weight depends on flake size and how the cup is filled. Pour them in loosely and level the top without shaking or pressing them down. Quick oats and steel-cut oats should not automatically use this value.

faq.q: Why does rolled oats weigh differently by cup?
faq.a: Brand, particle size, moisture, and how the cup is filled can change the result.

faq.q: Should I use a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Yes, a scale is the most repeatable option when baking precision matters.

name: White Rice (Uncooked)
note: Uncooked white rice is measured before cooking. Grain length, variety, and how it settles affect the weight in a cup. Fill a dry cup and level the surface without pressing. Do not use this value for cooked rice, which contains absorbed water.

faq.q: Why does white rice (uncooked) weigh differently by cup?
faq.a: Brand, particle size, moisture, and how the cup is filled can change the result.

faq.q: Should I use a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Yes, a scale is the most repeatable option when baking precision matters.

name: Cornstarch
note: Cornstarch is a fine powder that can compact in its container. Stir it gently, spoon it into a cup, and level it without pressing. In some regions cornflour means a different product, so confirm the package is pure corn starch.

faq.q: Why does cornstarch weigh differently by cup?
faq.a: Brand, particle size, moisture, and how the cup is filled can change the result.

faq.q: Should I use a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Yes, a scale is the most repeatable option when baking precision matters.
